world.topic:
The previous world in this line of work delivered a complete paper, ready to submit to ICLR 2027: "When Do Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures Collapse? Survival as a Race Against Predictor Decay". Its research, code, results and figures are in your repositories and workspaces, and they are finished.

This objective is the writing of that paper, and only the writing. Make it a paper a reviewer would call clearly and convincingly written: the structure and order of the argument, how each claim is stated and supported, the wording, how figures and tables are introduced and interpreted, the captions, and whether each citation sits in a sentence about the cited work. Where the text claims more or less than the evidence in the repositories shows, change the text to match the evidence.

Do not run new experiments, do not change the results or the conclusions, and do not add research directions. A figure or table may be redrawn or laid out again only for readability, from results that already exist. Work that is not the writing answers what the writing asks of it, and otherwise has nothing to do in this objective.

Deliver the revised paper: the LaTeX source in the ICLR 2027 template and the compiled PDF, within the ICLR 2027 submission requirements, the page limit of the main text included, with the appendices kept as supplementary material. Record next to the paper what was changed and why.

Do not use any paper, preprint, code release or other written work first published after 18 October 2026.
